title: #broadway #theatre #westend #greenscreen
transcript: are you actually frustrated by celebrity casting in theatre? or is it something else? I am gonna criticize it somewhat but first I'm gonna defend it cause like not to be annoying but I have quite literally seen hundreds and hundreds of examples of celebrity casting in theatre and I gotta be honest like 95% of the time they're actually quite good. I mean a huge portion of the time it's actually people who have a background in theater before getting their big movie or TV gig and even if not they're usually just like good actors who yes got the role without auditioning because of their fame but are nevertheless serious about the craft of acting, and contrary to popular belief, in my experience, screen acting skills do carry over to the stage way more often than not. and I think when celebrity casting is really done well there is a sense of care and craft in the production builtaround them almost a narrative in itself where a star collaborates to bring something to the stage that's important to them. like from what I can tell, most of y'all don't complain when the end result is actually good. and maybe that tells us something about where the root of this problem actually is. maybe you don't have a problem with celebrity casting maybe you have a problem with using celebrity casting as an excuse to put out subpar work and by the way charge a lot of money for it. I've been saying the same thing about jukebox musicals and movie to musical adaptations like I don't have a problem with adaptations or repurposing existing songs I have a problem with any show that feels soulless or tacky or using a stale formula. we're all actually talking about the same thing we're talking about producers don't care about the quality of product they're selling to you and I think it's more productive to focus on that root of the problem. there is another criticism I've heard about celebrity casting that I do think is valid which is that regardless of quality or talent it's not being harnessed in the best way. a lot of people have pointed out for example that Other Desert Cities could have still made a boatload of money with Julia Louis-Dreyfus alone or Small Mouth Sounds with Julia Roberts alone like you could cast up and comers in these supporting roles instead of playing celebrity Mad Libs with the entire cast. likewise we could be doing more of this: putting them in new plays instead of revivals. preferably new plays that are actually good and not poorly written vanity projects. and I agree it's frustrating to think that they could have their cake and eat it too; that they could make their money, attract their crowds and foster new talent at the same time. but these productions feel almost siloed even more so because of the ridiculous ticket prices pricing out most of the community. although I think that's more or less a battle that we've already lost. And the cynical part of me wants to say “who cares?” “just let Broadway keep digging itself into its capitalist hole” “at least there's still good theater off Broadway” “for those of us who care to pay attention.” but unfortunately I have to admit that the ecosystem is probably healthier when there is cross pollination. most immediately for the artists but eventually for audiences too. but now that ties back to the same point I was making about quality which is that the problem isn't just celebrities in shows it's how they're going about it
